mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS increases by at least 0.5% month-over-month, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in industrial production (INDPRO) reflects robust manufacturing activity and corporate capacity utilization, which supports higher corporate profits and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO increases by at least 0.3% month-over-month, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 5.0%, it signals a tight labor market that accelerates consumer spending and economic growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE is below 5.0, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) rises above 5.0%, it signals a tightening monetary policy that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is above 5.0, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: The joint increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals a strong labor market and robust consumer spending, which together drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when both PAYEMS and RSAFS increase by at least 0.3% month-over-month, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: The joint increase in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates a synchronized expansion in manufacturing and consumer housing demand, which together support corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when both INDPRO and HOUST increase by at least 0.5% month-over-month, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, an increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) leads to higher borrowing costs and reduced corporate investment, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods during monetary tightening cycles when FEDFUNDS rises, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, a GDP growth rate (GDPC1) above 3.5% annualized signals an overheating economy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the Fed may tighten policy.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods during late-cycle expansions when GDPC1 is above 3.5% annualized, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
